title: Writing and Balancing Equations; Combination and Decomposition

items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A painter's hissing bucket of quicklime opens the lesson: **how can we tell that a new substance is forming?**

Burning magnesium, a yellow precipitate and zinc fizzing in acid show the **signs of a chemical reaction**. Then we write reactions as **balanced equations**.

The bucket returns as a **combination** reaction; heat, electricity and sunlight break substances apart in **decomposition**.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• writing chemical formulae from valencies and ion charges

• the law of conservation of mass

• a chemical change forms a new substance

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** Identify chemical changes from observations.

**2.** Write word and skeletal equations and balance them, with state symbols.

**3.** Identify combination and decomposition (thermal, electrolytic, photolytic) reactions.

**4.** Tell exothermic from endothermic reactions.

items.text:
**What this shows**

• (a) A magnesium ribbon burning in air, held in tongs over a spirit lamp.

• (b) A colourless solution dropped into another colourless solution.

• (c) Zinc granules in dilute acid in a flask.

**Answer to Question 3**

Its **colour and state**: a new white substance, **magnesium oxide**, forms from magnesium and oxygen. The light and heat show energy given out.

**Answer to Question 4**

A **yellow solid**, lead iodide. An insoluble solid that forms in a solution is called a **precipitate**.

**Answer to Question 5**

**Bubbles of a gas** (hydrogen), and the flask feels warm: a **change in temperature**.

items.prompt: Which of these is a chemical change?
Barium chloride solution is added to sodium sulphate solution, and a white solid appears. This shows
options: evolution of a gas; the solid is barium chloride
a precipitate; the solid is barium sulphate
a change in colour; the solid is sodium chloride
a precipitate; the solid is sodium chloride

items.text:
**On Question 1**

A new substance with a sour taste forms; the other three form **no new substance**.

**On Question 2**

An insoluble solid that forms in a solution is a **precipitate**: here, white barium sulphate.

chunks.name: Writing a reaction as an equation

items.text:
**Answer to Question 6**

Write $\mathrm{2MgO}$ to balance oxygen (2 = 2). Magnesium is then 1 on the LHS and 2 on the RHS, so write $\mathrm{2Mg}$:

$\mathrm{2Mg}$ + $\mathrm{O_{2}}$ $\longrightarrow$ $\mathrm{2MgO}$

**What this shows**

Balancing iron and steam step by step. Each row is one step, with the number of atoms of each element on each side after it.

**Answer to Question 7(a)**

$\mathrm{Fe_{3}O_{4}}$, and its oxygen (4 atoms).

**Answer to Question 7(b)**

$\mathrm{H_{2}O_{4}}$ would be a different substance: only the coefficient changes.

items.prompt: Solutions of barium chloride and sodium sulphate react to give insoluble barium sulphate and a solution of sodium chloride. Complete the balanced equation: $\mathrm{BaCl_{2}(aq) + Na_{2}SO_{4}(aq)  \longrightarrow }$ ?

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**D**: 4 H atoms and 2 O atoms on each side. **B** changes the formula of water.

**On Question 2**

Barium sulphate is insoluble, so (s); sodium chloride stays dissolved, so (aq). $\mathrm{2NaCl}$ balances Na and Cl. **D** writes a wrong formula for sodium chloride.

**Answer to Question 8**

$\mathrm{CaO(s)}$ + $\mathrm{H_{2}O(l)}$ $\longrightarrow$ $\mathrm{Ca(OH)_{2}(aq)}$ + heat

**Answer to Question 9**

$\mathrm{Ca(OH)_{2}(aq)}$ + $\mathrm{CO_{2}(g)}$ $\longrightarrow$ $\mathrm{CaCO_{3}(s)}$ + $\mathrm{H_{2}O(l)}$

This takes two to three days. Marble is also $\mathrm{CaCO_{3}}$.

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**B**: one reactant breaks into two products.

**On Question 2**

A single product forms (**combination**), and heat and light are given out (**exothermic**).

items.text:
**What this shows**

• (a) Green ferrous sulphate crystals heated in a boiling tube.

• (b) Lead nitrate heated in a boiling tube.

• (c) Silver chloride in two dishes: one in the shade, one in sunlight.

**Answer to Question 10**

The crystals lose water and turn **reddish-brown** (ferric oxide); a **smell of burning sulphur** from the gases $\mathrm{SO_{2}}$ and $\mathrm{SO_{3}}$.

$\mathrm{2FeSO_{4}(s)}$ $\xrightarrow{\text{heat}}$ $\mathrm{Fe_{2}O_{3}(s)}$ + $\mathrm{SO_{2}(g)}$ + $\mathrm{SO_{3}(g)}$

**Answer to Question 11**

**Nitrogen dioxide**:

$\mathrm{2Pb(NO_{3})_{2}(s)}$ $\xrightarrow{\text{heat}}$ $\mathrm{2PbO(s)}$ + $\mathrm{4NO_{2}(g)}$ + $\mathrm{O_{2}(g)}$

**Answer to Question 12**

Light breaks silver chloride into **grey silver** and chlorine:

$\mathrm{2AgCl(s)}$ $\xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}}$ $\mathrm{2Ag(s)}$ + $\mathrm{Cl_{2}(g)}$

Silver bromide behaves the same way; this is used in black-and-white photography.

items.text:
**What this shows**

Water with a few drops of dilute sulphuric acid. Two carbon electrodes are joined to a battery, and each sits under a test tube, A or B, that collects gas.

**Answer to Question 13**

**B**, about twice as much as A. It is **hydrogen**, at the negative electrode; A holds oxygen.

$\mathrm{2H_{2}O(l)}$ $\xrightarrow{\text{electricity}}$ $\mathrm{2H_{2}(g)}$ + $\mathrm{O_{2}(g)}$: two $\mathrm{H_{2}}$ molecules for every $\mathrm{O_{2}}$.

Hydrogen burns with a pop sound; oxygen makes a candle burn more brightly.

items.prompt: In the electrolysis of water, $12\text{ mL}$ of oxygen is collected. How much hydrogen is collected in the same time?
During a reaction, the temperature of the mixture rises from $25\,^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $32\,^{\circ}\text{C}$. Classify, in order: this reaction, respiration, the decomposition of limestone.

items.text:
**On Question 1**

Hydrogen and oxygen form in the ratio **2 : 1** by volume: $2 \times 12 = 24\text{ mL}$.

**On Question 2**

The mixture warms, so heat is given out: **exothermic**. Respiration releases energy: **exothermic**. Breaking limestone apart takes in heat: **endothermic**.
